You know K and the starting amounts. You are asked for amounts at equilibrium. Pick the approach that goes from a known K to unknown concentrations.
The equilibrium constant puts products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient: \(K_c = \dfrac{[CO_2][H_2]}{[CO][H_2O]}\). Pick it from the Equations list.
Concentration is moles divided by liters. Divide each starting amount by the chamber's volume. Type the concentrations with M.
Step 1 is the direction. No products are present at the start, so the top of the reaction quotient is zero, and \(Q_c = 0\). Type Q.
Q is smaller than K, so the reaction proceeds to the right, toward the products. Pick that direction.

Step 2 is the ICE table. Initial: your starting concentrations, and 0 for both products. Change: \(-x\) for CO and H2O, \(+x\) for CO2 and H2, because every coefficient is 1. Equilibrium: initial plus change. Fill in the table.
Put the equilibrium row into \(K_c\): \(K_c = \dfrac{(x)(x)}{([CO]_0 - x)([H_2O]_0 - x)}\). Here the two starting concentrations are equal. Type it with your numbers.

Look at the shape before multiplying anything out. The top is \(x^2\), and because CO and H2O start equal, the bottom is \(([CO]_0 - x)^2\). Both are perfect squares, so take the square root of both sides. This shortcut works only because the two starting concentrations are equal. Pick that method.
Taking the positive square root gives \(\sqrt{K_c} = \dfrac{x}{[CO]_0 - x}\). Solve that for x. Type x.

A square root also has a negative value: \(-\sqrt{K_c} = \dfrac{x}{[CO]_0 - x}\). Solve it, and put that x into the equilibrium row. A root is physically meaningful only if every concentration comes out zero or positive. Say which root the chamber rejects, and why.
Step 3 ends with the equilibrium row: \([H_2] = x\). Type it with M.
Carbon monoxide at equilibrium is its starting concentration minus x. Type it with M.
Step 4 is the check. Put your equilibrium concentrations back into \(K_c\). You should get K back, within rounding. Type the value.

That shortcut needed equal starting concentrations. Would you like to see this same problem worked with less steam, so the two start unequal? Then the bottom is not a perfect square, and the quadratic formula takes over.
Put the equilibrium row into \(K_c\): \(K_c = \dfrac{x^2}{([CO]_0 - x)([H_2O]_0 - x)}\). This time the two starting concentrations differ. Type it with your numbers.

Look at the shape before multiplying anything out. The top is \(x^2\), but the bottom has two different factors, so it is not a perfect square, and the square root will not work. Multiply out, collect the terms into \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), and use the quadratic formula. Pick that method.
The quadratic formula, \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\), gives two roots. Keep the one that leaves every concentration zero or positive. Type x.
Put the other root into the equilibrium row. It is larger than one of the starting concentrations, so a reactant comes out negative. Say why the chamber rejects it.
